@graph.name: Crawl Presence Registry Dataset — Scope
@graph.description: What this registry is and the rules it runs on. Corpus presence is per-collection, era-tagged and method-honest: the registry joins three things — the Common Crawl collection list, the per-collection capture sets classified by URL class and content era, and the robots posture under which each crawl happened — so “what does the crawl hold about us” is a query result with dates, not folklore. The current estate (cutover 2026-10-28, per-route form 2026-10-31) is present in zero collections until a post-cutover collection carries it; everything the crawl holds today describes predecessor sites, and this registry says so in its era fields rather than letting the counts imply otherwise.

about.name: Corpus presence
about.description: The set of a domain’s captures inside open crawl collections (Common Crawl), from which public training/research corpora are built. Presence is observed per collection; it is never a standing or quality claim.

about.name: Content era
about.description: Each capture’s era — current-estate, pre-cutover-wordpress, wix-era, earlier-predecessor — computed by this generator from the capture timestamp against the 2026-10-28 cutover plus URL-form rules, never hand-tagged.

about.name: Robots posture as a recorded decision
about.description: The estate’s robots.txt posture is stored here as the owner’s decision (Option 1, open training, 2026-10-31) with the live file’s digest, and a drift gate fails generation and verification if the served file ever stops matching the recorded posture.

scopeRules: Query states come only from the controlled vocabulary (queried-clean / partial / unverifiable-index-error); a collection that could not be read is a visible row in that state, never an omission and never a zero.
Absence is recorded as an explicit zero capture count on a collection row; capture rows exist only for captures the index actually returned — no zero-filled or inferred capture rows.

Content era and URL class are computed by the generator from the URL form and capture timestamp; era contradictions (a predecessor URL form in a post-cutover capture, a current-estate form before the cutover) are flagged eraReview on the row, never silently classified.
Capture counts are observations about crawl coverage. No surface may render them as a standing, quality or authority claim (owner standard).
Historical capture rows are immutable: regeneration appends new observations; it never rewrites a prior collection’s rows.
The signal-observation log is append-only and hash-chained; each entry is signed with the estate key and verifiable against the published JWKS.

@graph.name: Crawl Presence Registry Dataset — Collections
@graph.description: Every collection in Common Crawl’s collinfo at seed time (129), each with its query state, the verbatim query method, the attempt count under the retry discipline, and the crawl window observed for this domain (first/last capture timestamps among this domain’s rows; where the domain returned no captures, no window is derivable and none is invented). 129 collections answered cleanly, 0 partially, 0 stand as unverifiable-index-error — visible states, retried on the cadence.

gapRecords.title: The current estate has zero corpus presence; its debut is a single upcoming collection that nothing was scheduled to observe
evidence: Dossier 05 §2.1 — full-method index sweep: every collection crawled to date predates the 2026-10-28 cutover, so the current estate is present in zero collections by date arithmetic
This registry’s seed sweep (2026-10-31): newest collection in collinfo is CC-MAIN-2026-43; current-era captures observed: 0
gapRecords.impact: Until a post-cutover collection carries the estate, every corpus built from Common Crawl teaches the predecessor WordPress site.
gapRecords.solution: The November watch, as a standing instrument: on the measurement cadence, poll collinfo; the day a post-CC-MAIN-2026-43 collection appears, run the wildcard query against it and write the debut record into this registry (classes, statuses, digests, timestamps). If a collection misses the domain, the escalation is supply-side only — verify CCBot-facing health and link inflow, record missed-collection, and let the next check be a second observation; two consecutive misses escalate to a named finding in the cadence report.

gapRecords.title: Presence, when it comes, will be a sample — which URL classes the frontier samples is unobservable in advance and was unrecorded after the fact
evidence: Dossier 05 §1.1 (per-domain caps) + §2.2 (the October frontier over-sampled taxonomy URLs)
gapRecords.impact: The corpus value of the estate concentrates in its densest texts (datasets, llms-full, graphs, deep pages); a sample that lands on thin URLs wastes the cycle.
gapRecords.solution: URL-class accounting in this registry (the presence_summary view): after the debut collection, state the sampled mix as data. If the mix starves the dense classes, the designed response is internal-link and sitemap-priority emphasis on those files from high-authority pages — the one frontier input we control — with the next collection’s mix as the test. No response is designed for a mix that has not been observed.
gapRecords.status: open — the accounting is built into this registry; the first sampled-mix observation awaits the first post-cutover collection

gapRecords.title: The training-data posture was a blanket allow that had never been recorded as a decision
evidence: Dossier 05 §2.3 — the live file’s full contents: every major training crawler named-allowed or wildcard-allowed; no Disallow lines
gapRecords.impact: Coherence with the distribution thesis is not the same as a recorded choice; training admission is effectively irrevocable for already-published collections.
gapRecords.solution: A one-page decision record with three options and their mechanics, presented to the owner; the chosen option executed exactly as chosen and stored in this registry’s robots_policy record with the file’s digest, so any future drift between the recorded posture and the live file is a gate failure, not an opinion.
gapRecords.status: resolved — owner decision recorded 2026-10-31: Option 1, open training, made deliberate. No file change (Option 1 mechanics); the policy gate is armed in verify.js §22 and in this generator’s drift gate

gapRecords.title: Filter survival is reasoned, not measured — no extracted (WET) record of this domain’s pages has ever been read
evidence: Dossier 05 §1.2/§2.4 — the filter reading is inference throughout; no WET record of any estate page has been inspected
gapRecords.impact: “Our pages survive corpus filtering” is currently a likelihood, not a fact, per URL class.
gapRecords.solution: The WET inspection, scheduled against the debut capture: pull WET records for a fixed sample (homepage, one category page, one dataset file, llms.txt, one blog post) via the index’s offset/length pointers and score extraction completeness, boilerplate share and repeated-line fraction into this registry’s filter_inspection table; any structural problem becomes a designed estate fix in the normal batch motion.
gapRecords.status: open — awaits the first current-estate capture (P1); the filter_inspection table stands empty by design until then

gapRecords.title: Stale-corpus dilution has no counterweight: the predecessor sites’ text sits in dozens of collections and is re-ingested by future corpus builds
evidence: Dossier 05 §2.1 — the 2025-and-earlier sweep: predecessor captures across many collections (this registry’s per-era totals carry the current count)
gapRecords.impact: Bounded but real: historical snapshots are genuinely used by corpus builders, and the old text’s service claims and framing are superseded.
gapRecords.solution: Dilution by supply, the only mechanism that exists (published collections are immutable research artifacts — there is no correction channel): maximize the current estate’s presence in new collections (P1/P2), keep URLs stable so recaptures accumulate on the same URLs, and record the staleness honestly in this registry’s content-era fields so no program document claims the corpus “knows” the current company until P1+P4 say so.
gapRecords.status: open — measured per collection by this registry; closes by accumulation as post-cutover collections land

gapRecords.title: Four 2026 collections could not be verified in the dossier pass because the index API errored under load
evidence: Dossier 05 §2.1/§8 — 502/504 responses recorded per collection (2026-25, -21, -17, -04 unverified at dossier time)
gapRecords.impact: A registry seeded with silent gaps inherits them; the holes were pre-rebuild, so no current-estate verdict depended on them.
gapRecords.solution: The registry’s seed sweep runs with retry/back-off until every collection returns a definitive answer (captures or “No Captures”), and any collection that still cannot be read is seeded as unverifiable-index-error — a visible state, not an omission. The cadence runner inherits the same discipline: an errored check is reported as errored, never as “no change.”

@graph.name: Crawl Presence Registry — Method
@graph.description: How the registry is built and maintained. (1) A seed sweep queries every Common Crawl collection in collinfo for the domain wildcard, 2026 series first, under a retry/back-off discipline; each collection’s answer — captures, a clean “No Captures”, a partial read, or an index error after all retries — is frozen as the generator’s seed with the verbatim method and attempt counts. (2) URL class and content era are computed from the returned rows by fixed rules (URL-form marker lists; capture timestamp vs the 2026-10-28 cutover); contradictions are flagged, not smoothed. (3) The robots policy is parsed from the deployed source file, and generation fails if the served file’s digest — carried by the signed signal observation — differs from the source’s: the drift gate. (4) Signal observations are appended by observing, digest-chaining and signing; historical entries are never edited. (5) Cadence: monthly, aligned to collection releases, plus a run whenever collinfo gains a collection; every regeneration re-seals the file in the estate’s signed index in the same motion.
articleBody: Transport note (2026-10-31): the seed sweep’s queries were carried by curl after the Python HTTP client hung against the index through this environment’s proxy path; the method string on every collection row states the query itself, which is identical either way, and the attempt counts are the real ones.

Era classification disclosure: URL-form markers govern (Wix forms, then WordPress forms). Unmarked pre-cutover captures are classed pre-cutover-wordpress in the 2024-and-later window — the SiteGround WordPress site was the continuously operating predecessor then — and earlier-predecessor before it. The rule is uniform and stated here so any row can be re-derived; rows whose form contradicts their timestamp carry eraReview instead of a quiet verdict.

The 2026-43 full count: the dossier recorded a floor (≥25 in the first response page) because its full-count queries errored; this registry’s seed sweep completed the query, and the capture rows here are the full returned set for every collection whose query state is queried-clean.

@graph.name: Crawl Presence Registry — Boundaries
@graph.description: What this registry will not do. It never presents a capture count — ours or anyone’s — as a standing, quality or authority signal; counts here are crawl-coverage observations with dates. It never records a capture, a window, a snapshot or an adherence claim it did not observe: unverifiable states are rows, absences are zeros on collection rows, and unrun checks are labeled not-checked. It never edits the recorded past: historical rows and signed observations are immutable. It makes no claim about private or licensed corpora, which publish no membership. And it does not decide posture: the training decision is the owner’s, recorded here exactly as made (Option 1, 2026-10-31) and enforced by the drift gate, never editorialized.
boundaryRules: No-count-as-standing rule: capture counts are observations, never quality or authority signals.
No-invention rule: an unobserved value is an explicit state (unverifiable-index-error / not-checked / absent), never a filled-in value.
Immutability rule: published collections and signed observations are history; corrections arrive as new observations, never edits.
Open-ecosystem scope rule: private/licensed corpora are named as beyond measurement, not guessed at.
Owner-decision rule: posture changes only by a recorded owner decision; drift between the live file and the recorded decision is a gate failure.
